active.F_167.py: fman_pcd.c: F-167 — standalone FMFP_EXTC (FPM External Requests Control, CCSR 0x074) SYNC probe. DPAA RM §5.12.14.1 documents this register's INV0 bit as required by all three officially-documented Custom Classifier table update flows; fman_pcd_ehash_add_key() has never asserted it -- a candidate for both the ehash MISS and the AC_CC/FE_ENTER port-wedge. Adds an inert-by-default debugfs node (fe_extc: cat reads the register, 'echo sync' asserts INV0 and polls for HW to clear it) so the register can be tested standalone without engaging any port. Purely additive; does not touch fman_pcd_ehash_add_key() or any existing fe_* code path.

F-167 board-confirmed the register is safe/responsive to touch standalone (echo sync > fe_extc on .185, zero adverse effect, repeated twice); F-168 is the first test with an actual port arm in the picture, testing whether SYNC prevents the port-wedge that has reproducibly occurred on every prior AC_CC arm attempt this session. active.F_169.py: fman_pcd.c: F-169 — debugfs verb (fe_kg_ekfc: 'set <scheme_id_hex> <ekfc_hex>') to reconfigure a live KeyGen scheme's EKFC. T-M3-R attempt 1 (genuine ehash HIT test) stalled with a real harness gap found: KeyGen scheme4 was never reconfigured off its own 12-byte CC-tree EKFC (0x00180006) to match the 14-byte ehash table's format (F-163's 0x801C0006) before the FE_ENTER-direct arm. The existing fman_pcd_kg_scheme_set_ekfc() (fman_pcd_kg.c) has zero callers because it's buggy -- a single enable=true call against an already-bound scheme is rejected by keygen_scheme_setup()'s own used-scheme guard. F-169 implements the correct disable/mutate/re-enable sequence fresh, directly against fman->keygen->schemes[] via the module-internal fman_keygen_internal.h (designed for exactly this kind of sibling-translation-unit access). Purely additive; only fires on an explicit set write, intended to run immediately before fe_arm engage.
active.F_171.py: fman_pcd.c: F-171 — adds a `fe_group` debugfs verb that wraps the existing FE_ENTER chain (built by `fe_enter build`) in a genuine CONT_LOOKUP group AD (RM §8.7.4.1/§7.11: numKeys=1, matchTableAddr, adTableAddr, keySize=16) with an all-wildcard match row (mask=0x00 on every byte), instead of writing FE_ENTER directly to FMBM_RCCB as every off!=0 T-M3-R arm this session has done — the deprecated 'RCCB→FE_ENTER direct' topology the RM says was superseded 2026-07-16. The all-wildcard mask sidesteps F-158's still-open CC-compare-window-layout question entirely: any frame reaching this group AD trivially matches regardless of byte order, and dispatches into the already-built, already-byte-verified FE_ENTER chain. `echo "build <miss_fqid_hex>" > fe_group` builds match table (64B) + AD table (32B, ato[0]=verbatim copy of fe_enter's root AD, ato[1]=miss-AD) + the 16B group AD itself; `cat fe_group` shows the group AD's own offset, which is what gets passed to the existing `fe_arm engage <port> <offset> <fqid>` instead of fe_enter's own root_ad offset. Purely additive; fe_arm itself is unmodified.
active.F_172.py: fman_pcd.c: F-172 — extends F-171's `fe_group` write handler to accept an explicit 16-byte key + 16-byte mask (`echo "build <miss_fqid_hex> <32-hex key> <32-hex mask>" > fe_group`), instead of always programming the all-wildcard match row F-171 hardcoded. Motivation: F-171's wildcard test armed cleanly but a discriminator test proved it does not distinguish HIT from MISS (ping and the matching SYN both dispatched to the same FQID regardless of match). Documentation review found the only prior real-key test of this dispatch shape, F-158 (2026-08-01, real key + full participate-mask via `cc_test`, decisive-negative result), predates F-168's FMFP_EXTC SYNC fix (2026-08-06, board-confirmed to fix a real dispatch defect) — so a real key + real mask has never been tried with F-168 present. Adds `fman_pcd_fe_group_hex2bin()` (self-contained hex parser, no kernel hex2bin() dependency) and widens `fman_pcd_fe_group_build()`'s signature to `(pcd, miss_fqid, key, mask)`; `key`/`mask` NULL reproduces F-171's original wildcard default exactly (fully backward compatible). Purely additive on top of F-171; no other fe_* verb or struct field touched.
active.F_178.py: fman_pcd_kg.c: F-178 (2026-08-07), written in direct response to the user's challenge: vendor's real ASK code demonstrably works on this exact board/microcode, so what does this project's own approach do differently? Full read of vendor's real FM_PORT_SetPCD()/SetPcd() documents that for a single-bound-scheme port, vendor ALWAYS ORs NIA_KG_DIRECT | physicalSchemeId into fmbm_rfpne -- without it, KeyGen falls back to the generic SI/match-vector walk (RM sec 4.4) instead of deterministically dispatching to the CC-attached scheme. F-162 (2026-08-05) already found and fixed exactly this gap once, but wired the fix ONLY into fman_pcd_kg_port_attach_cc()/detach_cc() -- the CONT_LOOKUP/group-AD 'CC-graft' mechanism this project's own history has since abandoned. The ACTUAL arm path every T-M3-R test has ever used, fman_pcd_kg_port_arm_fe()/_disarm_fe() (patch 0132), is a separate function pair that reprograms the scheme's next_engine and calls fman_port_set_cc_base(), but NEVER calls F-162's own fman_port_set_kg_direct_scheme() helper -- confirmed directly by this session's own dmesg on every single arm ('rfpne 0x00480200', never '... | NIA_KG_DIRECT | scheme_id'). This means every carefully-configured EKFC/key-format/hash_bytes_offset/PORT_ID value this project has tested on 'scheme 4' may never have actually been consulted for live traffic, if the generic SI/match-vector walk selects a different scheme (or none) instead. Fix: call fman_port_set_kg_direct_scheme(rxport, id) (F-162's existing, already-CI-wired helper -- id already in scope via kg_find_port_scheme()) at the end of arm_fe()'s success path, symmetric fman_port_clear_kg_direct_scheme(rxport) in disarm_fe(). No new register-level code -- two new call sites reusing F-162's own verified mechanism. Dry-run tested (including idempotency) against the exact reconstructed source text before commit.
active.F_179.py: fman_keygen.c: F-179 (2026-08-07), follow-up while resolving <combine>/PORT_ID against vendor's real, pristine FMC compiler source (github.com/nxp-qoriq/fmc @ 5b9f4b16a864e9dfa58cdcc860be278a7f66ac18, the exact commit this project's own fmc_git.bb pins). That trace definitively found <combine> builds KeyGen's extractedOrs (FQID-only), correcting an earlier doc claim it was a GEC key mechanism -- and while closing out that context, found KG_SCH_KN_PORT_ID (EKFC bit 31, the real key-extraction path, unrelated to <combine>) draws its value from kgse_dv0/kgse_dv1 (fm_pcd_ext.h's t_FmPcdExtractEntry has no dedicated union member for PORT_PRIVATE_INFO; vendor's fm_kg.c BuildSchemeRegs() assigns kgse_dv0/dv1 straight from the scheme's privateDflt0/1 fields). This project's own fman_keygen.c (mainline-derived, unmodified for this logic) populates kgse_dv0/dv1 with DEFAULT_HASH_KEY_IPv4_ADDR/DEFAULT_HASH_KEY_L4_PORT (0x0A0A0A0A/0x0B0B0B0B) inside the `if (scheme->use_hashing)` branch -- an unrelated mainline RSS-hashing-fallback mechanism. Live-read on .185 scheme 4 confirmed an exact byte-for-byte match. This project's own EKFC override never reprograms these registers, so both existing PORT_ID board measurements (the 2026-07-13 184,320-candidate brute force and the 2026-08-07 16-candidate 0x00-0x0f sweep) were run against this uncontrolled value -- neither result can be trusted to rule the mechanism out. Fix: zero kgse_dv0/kgse_dv1/kgse_ekdv whenever this project's own EKFC override (scheme->ekfc) is in control, so any PORT_ID extraction reads a known 0x00 instead of a leftover RSS constant, making a portid=0x00 retest genuinely controlled for the first time. Dry-run tested (including idempotency) against the exact reconstructed source text before commit.

active.F_185.py: fman_pcd.c/fman_pcd_kg.c/fman_pcd_internal.h: F-185 (2026-08-12, E23) -- vendor-faithful CC dispatch: AC_CC mode + VARIANT B en_exthash_node at RCCB, the NXP ASK SDK production path (user-approved direction after the E23 Ghidra decode). The 210.10.1 CC engine's single AD-type extraction site (c600001e >>30 @ w1857, br_tbl[0xf000]) routes type-1 CONT_LOOKUP into the enhanced external-hash machine, which parses the 16B RCCB AD as an en_exthash_node VARIANT B (word0: table_hi:8|ipv4_ad_off:8|hash_bytes_off:3|rsv|table_type:4|key_size:6|miss_action:2; word1: table_base_lo; word2: mask_bits:4|global_mem_off:12|pool:16; word3: miss NIA) -- field widths proven by the microcode's own extraction census (w1711 AND-0x3f, w1610 AND-0xff, w1598 AND-0xf, w1557 >>16, table_lo staged dmem[0xe000] w2045/2049, bucket_index w1928 off KG hash ctx[0xd048]), and the .106 production row (tcp4 4e400008 eb700100 0402080f 00480308) decodes VARIANT B 4 independent ways incl. word3 = NIA_ENG_KG|NIA_KG_CC_EN|NIA_KG_DIRECT|scheme and word1 = the probed DDR bucket array. ROOT CAUSE of F-183's silicon result (frames consumed, no canary, no delivery): the RM-8.7.4.1 group AD parses as a GARBAGE node (miss_action DONE, keysize 0, table_base 0x56f00 = MURAM offset misread as DDR physical, pool 0x4F0000 out of range) -> every frame terminated with no disposition; there is no match-table walker in this blob, only the external-hash machine. The historical AC_CC stalls (0118 iter-48, Path A 08-10, E20) were invalid-CONTENT stalls, not invalid-MODE: a bare FE_ENTER at RCCB parses as a node with table_base=0, pool=0 -> pool-0 workspace wait = the silent-WAIT signature; .106 runs AC_CC (12 schemes 0x8x000006, ccbs=0, 0% loss under load) on this identical blob. 6 blocks: (1) engage scaffold writes the VARIANT B node at gro -- word0 (1<<30)|(key_size<<24)|(4<<20)|(hash_shift<<16)|table_hi, word1 table_dma lo, word2 ((fe_int_buf_off>>8)<<16)|(0x80<<4)|mask_bits, word3 0 placeholder -- needing the fe_ehash table + fe_int_buf pool, falling back to F-183's numKeys=0 miss-enq group when either is absent (production pass-through preserved); (2) new fman_pcd_fe_node_set_miss_nia() writing word3 (no-op unless the node form was built); (3) fman_pcd_internal.h declaration; (4) arm_fe next_engine 2->3 (AC_CC, mode 0x80000006, CCOBASE=0) + cc_bits_sel=0 (vendor ccbs=0 in AC_CC mode); (5) miss-NIA commit 0x00480000|0x00000200|0x00000100|scheme_id (byte-exact the .106 0x0048030x encoding) after scheme-id resolution, before fman_port_set_cc_base() asserts EXTC SYNC; (6) ENGAGED dmesg text. HIT = the DDR entry's opcode script ENQUEUE_PKT -> param.fqid (F-181/F-182 vendor-faithful records); MISS = word3 NIA -> KG-direct re-entry with CC_EN -> scheme fqb enqueue -> kernel. Teardown unchanged (detach_cc -> next_engine=0, word3 cleared via F-051 zeroing; set_cc_base(0) clears RCCB + rfpne CC_EN). Anchored on exact F-183/F-184 derived outputs; runs after both.
active.F_186.py: fman_pcd.c/fman_pcd_kg.c: F-186 (2026-08-12, E25 silicon-proof, .185 6.18.44-vyos, live /dev/mem validated) -- correct the F-185 node miss-action. E24/E25 proved the F-185 miss form (miss_action_type=NIA, word0 bits[31:30]=0b01, word3 = KG|DIRECT|CC_EN|scheme NIA) is FATAL on the 210.10.1 blob: empty-bucket MISS -> word3 NIA -> full KG re-classification into the AC_CC scheme -> node -> MISS -> NIA = INFINITE LOOP (spc ~4.5M classifications/sec sustained for minutes, no hop limit, no stall, frames never terminate; recovery = fe_arm disengage); KG-direct to a FOREIGN scheme instead -> FM_FD_ERR_NO_SCHEME (0x00004000) -> port error FQ 0x291 (dmesg 'Err FD status = 0x00004000'). CORRECT form (999 patch ExternalHashTableSet e_FM_PCD_DONE case, EN_EHASH_MISS_ACTION_ENQUE=2, and E25 live-verified): word0 bits[31:30] = 0b10 (ENQUE) + word3 = fqid (the nia/fqid union) = DIRECT ENQUEUE, no KG, loop-free; E25: ENQUE + own-port fqb 0x300 delivers to the kernel (curl rc=7, spc stable at 2). E25 also proved the miss fqid MUST be the frame's own-port base fqid: cross-port fqb (0x200/eth3) delivers to eth3's FQ but the dpaa driver drops it (eth3 rx_dropped++; the FD's buffer belongs to the frame's own BM pool). 2 blocks: (1) fman_pcd.c engage node word0 -> (2U<<30) ENQUE (fallback RM group untouched); (2) fman_pcd_kg.c arm_fe captures u32 miss_fqid = slot->base_fqid under the lock (before mutex_unlock) and commits it as node word3 via fman_pcd_fe_node_set_miss_nia(pcd, fe_enter_off, miss_fqid) instead of the KG-direct NIA -- lands before fman_port_set_cc_base() asserts EXTC SYNC. bpid INTENTIONALLY NOT changed (record keeps bpid=0): bpid=0 to the own-port fqb was never cleanly tested in E25 (all bpid=1 HIT runs were live /dev/mem patches), so whether the machine uses the record's param.bpid on the ENQUEUE_PKT path is an open single-variable E26 matrix test; if it matters it becomes F-187. HIT path unchanged (F-181/F-182 opcode script, verified delivering in E25). Anchored on the exact F-185 derived output; runs after F-185.
active.F_188.py: fman_pcd.c: F-188 (2026-08-12, P0-2 production-path audit; decomp/experiments.md E28) -- align the production genl/flowtable path with the E25/E26-verified 14-byte ehash mechanism. Three stale bits guaranteed no production HIT: (1) __fman_pcd_fe_build_vm_chain() created the ehash table with ehash_key_sz=13 and fman_pcd_fe_engage() armed EKFC 0x001C0006 (13-byte, no PORT_ID) while the flow records are 14-byte (ASK_FE_KEY_SIZE=14, F-163) -- comparator byte-count and bucket index can never agree; (2) fman_pcd_fe_flow_add() wrote param.fqid = action->enq_off, fed by ask.ko's ask_hw_get_enq_fe_off() = fman_pcd_fe_enq_get_offset() = the ENQ FE's MURAM offset (an invalid FQID; the E25/E26 finding says the target must be the frame's OWN-port RX FQID, 0x300/eth4 -- cross-port enqueues drop in the dpaa driver); (3) ask_fe_build_key() wrote k[0] = key->port_id (the FMan hw port id, 0x11/eth4) but the silicon's PORT_ID extraction reads the zeroed dv0/dv1 default = 0x00 (2026-08-06 brute force + E25/E26) -- fixed by a direct OOT edit to kernel/ask/oot-modules/ask/ask_flow_offload.c (k[0]=0, v4 + v6). F-188 itself (4 blocks, fman_pcd.c): ehash_key_sz 13->14, the v6-table 'Same EKFC' comment, fe_engage EKFC 0x001C0006->0x801C0006, and fe_flow_add target -> fman_pcd_resolve_miss_fqid(pcd, hw_port_id) (the same params-page default RX FQID the miss path uses). Verified live pre-fix: the genl engage already reaches the F-185/F-186 arm (RCCB 8d400000 fa180000 04c7080f 00000300 = ENQUE node + own-port miss fqid + mask 0x7fff + dv0/dv1=0), so only the three bits were stale. Also found: the nft flowtable offload is blocked on this board by passive conntrack (nf_conntrack_count stays 0 even with active forwarding) -- production-path HIT validation must drive ask_fe_flow_insert via a conntrack-active flowtable or a REPLACE-unit test (separate item). Anchored on the exact post-F-187 derived state; runs after F-187.
